title: Chapter 39 — First Night-Watch
paragraphs: Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha! Ahem! Let me clear my throat! I've been thinking about it ever since, and that laugh is the final conclusion. Why? Because a laugh is the wisest, easiest answer to everything that's strange. And come what may, one comfort always remains: it's all predestined. I didn't hear all his talk with Starbuck, but to my eye, Starbuck looked the way I felt the other evening. You can be sure the old sultan has got him, too. I caught it, knew it — if I had the gift, I could have prophesied it easily. Because when I got a good look at his skull, I saw it. Well, Stubb, wise Stubb — that's my title — well, Stubb, what of it? Here's a body. I don't know all that may be coming, but whatever it is, I'll go to meet it laughing. What a mischievous leer lurks in all your horrors! I feel funny. Fa la! La la! What's my sweet little wife doing at home right now? Crying her eyes out? Giving a party for the latest harpooners, I'd wager, cheerful as a ship's pennant, and so am I — fa la! La la! Oh —
We'll drink tonight with hearts as light, to love, as gay and fleeting as bubbles that swim on the beaker's brim, and break on the lips while meeting.
A brave song that — who calls? Mr. Starbuck? Yes, yes, sir — (Aside) he's my superior, and he has his too, if I'm not mistaken. — Yes, yes, sir, just finishing this job — coming.
